title: To Calosyrium on the Anthropomorphic God
english: Arriving from Mount Kalamos, some were asked by me about the monks there, what manner of life they lead, or what conduct of life they have.
They said that they prosper in much asceticism, and greatly desire to achieve the monastic life that befits the monks.
But they said that there are some who pass by and disturb those who wish to be quiet, and they assured themselves by arguing such things.
For they said that since the human is to be made according to the image of God, the divine Scripture says, one must believe that the divine is either humanlike or anthropomorphic.
Which is completely absurd, and able to be charged with the stains of the last impiety to those who think thus.
For the human is acknowledged to be according to the image of God, but the likeness is not physical.
And the Savior himself teaches this, saying 'God is Spirit.'
Therefore, if he is spirit, he is not in a physical form.
translator_notes: The Greek text is a fragment; the first paragraph ends mid-sentence with 'οὐδὲ ἐν εἴδει σωματικῷ.'
The phrase 'ἀνθρωποειδὲς ἤγουν ἀνθρωπομορφόν' is a gloss within the text explaining the terms.
The reference to 'the last impiety' (ἐσχάτης δυσσεβείας) is a reference to the final age of apostasy.
